summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with recurrent primary central nervous system B-cell lymphoma was admitted electively for his 27th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. Admission labs revealed a persistently low white blood cell count (2.7), which contraindicated chemotherapy due to infection risk. The cause was unclear but likely related to prior treatment or possible bone marrow involvement. He remained on Keppra for seizure control and was started on lamotrigine for improved prophylaxis. Airborne precautions were initiated due to a positive PPD and family history of TB but discontinued after a chest X-ray showed only old granulomatous changes without active disease. He was discharged home with instructions to continue all home medications, monitor for rash on lamotrigine, and attend an outpatient bone marrow biopsy to evaluate the cause of leukopenia before resuming chemotherapy.
